u0452.gist: Japan's JAXA launched the MMX mission on 20 October 2026 to achieve the world's first sample return from the Martian system.
facts: Launched 20 October 2026 on H3 Flight No. 10 from Tanegashima Space Center, Japan.
Studies Mars's two moons, Phobos and Deimos; will return at least 10 grams from Phobos.
Arrival at Mars expected 2027; samples reach Earth in 2031; planned duration about five years.
Key question: are the moons captured asteroids or debris from a giant impact on Mars?
Carries 13 instruments; rover IDEFIX built jointly by France's CNES and Germany's DLR.
NASA gives MEGANE spectrometer, P-Sampler and Deep Space Network; NASA gets about 15% of samples.
u0452.trap: Samples come from Phobos, not Deimos. JAXA's C-Sampler takes subsurface material; NASA's P-Sampler takes surface particles.

mcq.q: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched by JAXA in October 2026 aims to return samples from which moon?
mcq.why: MMX will return at least 10 grams of material from Phobos.

u0453.gist: In late June 2026, an IndiGo Airbus A321 made India's first satellite-based landing approach by a commercial jet, using the indigenous GAGAN system.
facts: DGCA supervised India's first Satellite-Based Landing System (SLS) approach in late June 2026.
Aircraft: IndiGo Airbus A321; used satellite guidance instead of an Instrument Landing System (ILS).
GAGAN = GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation; built by ISRO and Airports Authority of India.
Ground network: 15 reference stations (INRES), 2 master control centres (INMCC), 3 uplink stations (INLUS).
3 geostationary satellites carry GAGAN payloads; 4 communication networks link the stations.
NavIC gives positioning and timing; GAGAN corrects GPS for precise aircraft landing.
u0453.hook: GAGAN ground count 15-2-3: 15 stations watch, 2 centres compute, 3 stations send up.
u0453.trap: GAGAN only improves (augments) GPS signals; NavIC is India's own regional navigation satellite system.

mcq.q: GAGAN, used in India's first satellite-based landing approach by a commercial jet in 2026, was developed by ISRO along with which body?
mcq.why: GAGAN was developed by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India; DGCA only supervised the demonstration.

u0454.gist: The US made SOLAR-1 operational on June 10, 2026; it is the first US satellite built only for continuous space-weather observation.
facts: Operational on June 10, 2026; operated by NOAA (National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration).
Its data goes to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) for forecasts and alerts.
SOLAR-1 = Space Weather Observations at L1 to Advance Readiness–1; earlier name SWFO-L1.
It orbits the Sun–Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1).
Launched September 24, 2025 on a SpaceX Falcon 9 from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Final engine burn on January 23, 2026, after about four months and nearly one million miles.
u0454.hook: SOLAR-1 sits at L1: both carry a '1'.
u0454.trap: Launched in 2025 (September 24) but made operational in 2026 (June 10).

mcq.q: SOLAR-1, made operational in June 2026 as the first US satellite only for space-weather observation, orbits around which point?
mcq.why: It was renamed SOLAR-1 after reaching its orbit around Sun–Earth Lagrange Point 1.

u0455.gist: On May 18, 2026, ISRO scientists reported ChaSTE data after the Vikram lander's 'hop', showing layered moon soil near the south pole.
facts: Report shared May 18, 2026 on Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander 'hop' experiment.
Vikram reignited its engines and landed nearly 50 cm away, testing ascent for future sample return.
ChaSTE (Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment) is a lunar thermometer, re-inserted into the regolith (moon soil).
Found a two-layer structure in the top 6.5 cm of soil at the post-hop site.
Soil gets denser and stickier with depth; craters made temperatures drop faster (shadowing effect).
The engine firing blew away the top 3 cm of regolith.
u0455.hook: Hop 50 cm, blew off 3 cm, found layers in 6.5 cm.

mcq.q: During Chandrayaan-3's 'hop' experiment (findings shared in May 2026), about how far from its first position did the Vikram lander land?
mcq.why: Vikram reignited its engines and landed nearly 50 cm away from its initial position.

u0456.gist: On 4 May 2026, Pixxel and Sarvam partnered to build Pathfinder, India's first orbital data centre satellite, which will run AI in space.
facts: Announced 4 May 2026: Pixxel–Sarvam strategic partnership for Pathfinder.
Pixxel will design, build, launch and operate it, and give the hyperspectral imaging payload.
Sarvam gives the AI backbone: India-built language models running on the satellite's GPUs.
Orbital data centre = satellites with data-centre-class GPUs that run AI in orbit (like edge computing).
Pathfinder is a single-satellite demonstrator, built at Pixxel's Gigapixxel facility (up to 100 units).
u0456.hook: Pixxel = pictures and the satellite body; Sarvam = the AI brain.

mcq.q: Pathfinder, announced in May 2026 as India's first orbital data centre satellite, is a partnership between Pixxel and which company?
mcq.why: Pixxel builds and operates Pathfinder; Sarvam provides the AI backbone.

u0457.gist: NASA's Artemis II, launched April 1, 2026, was a crewed lunar flyby, not a landing: first humans near the Moon since 1972.
facts: Lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026; first crewed Artemis flight.
Crewed lunar flyby: humans near the Moon for the first time in 53 years.
Tested NASA's Space Launch System and Orion spacecraft; the crew named Orion 'Integrity'.
Orion's heat shield worked as expected; char loss much lower than in Artemis I.
The last crewed Moon mission before this was Apollo 17 in 1972, which landed.
Artemis III: listed for 2027 as a low-Earth-orbit test of SpaceX and Blue Origin landers.
u0457.trap: Artemis II = flyby only (no landing); Apollo 17 (1972) = landing.

mcq.q: What name did the crew give to the Orion spacecraft used in NASA's Artemis II mission (2026)?
mcq.why: The Orion spacecraft used in Artemis II was named Integrity by the crew.

u0458.gist: ISRO, ASI and IAA held SMOPS-2026, the second International Conference on Spacecraft Mission Operations, in Bengaluru on 8-10 April 2026.
facts: Second edition, SMOPS-2026, held 8 to 10 April 2026 in Bengaluru.
Organisers: ISRO, Astronautical Society of India (ASI), International Academy of Astronautics (IAA).
Theme: 'Innovative Operations for Smart and Sustainable Space Mission Management – Next Generation'.
Inaugurated on 8 April 2026 by A. S. Kiran Kumar, former Chairman of ISRO.
u0458.trap: SMOPS-2026 was the second edition, not the first.

mcq.q: SMOPS-2026, the second International Conference on Spacecraft Mission Operations, was held in which city?
mcq.why: SMOPS-2026 was held from 8 to 10 April 2026 in Bengaluru.

u0459.gist: Union Budget 2026-27 backs four astronomy facilities: NLST and NLOT in Ladakh, an upgraded Himalayan Chandra Telescope, and COSMOS-2 planetarium at Amaravati.
facts: NLST (National Large Solar Telescope): Merak near Pangong Lake, Ladakh; 2-metre class; studies the Sun.
NLOT (National Large Optical–Infrared Telescope): Hanle, Ladakh; 13.7-metre segmented primary mirror.
Himalayan Chandra Telescope (HCT), Hanle: 2-metre telescope; first light 26 September 2000.
HCT is operated remotely from CREST near Bengaluru; upgrade planned to a 3.7-metre telescope.
COSMOS-2 Planetarium: at Amaravati, implemented by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
u0459.hook: Merak = Sun (Solar telescope by Pangong Lake); Hanle = night sky (NLOT + HCT).
u0459.trap: NLST (Solar) is at Merak; NLOT (Optical–Infrared) is at Hanle. One letter apart.

mcq.q: Under Union Budget 2026-27, where will the National Large Solar Telescope (NLST) be built?
mcq.why: The NLST will be built at Merak near Pangong Lake, Ladakh.

mcq.q: The proposed National Large Optical–Infrared Telescope (NLOT) at Hanle will have a primary mirror of what size?
mcq.why: NLOT will have a 13.7-metre segmented primary mirror.

u0460.gist: On January 21, 2026, IN-SPACe signed with the Pixxel-led 'Allied Orbits' consortium to build India's first indigenous commercial Earth Observation satellite constellation.
facts: Agreement formalised January 21, 2026 by IN-SPACe under the EO-PPP programme.
Pixxel Space (Bengaluru) leads; members: Piersight Space, SatSure Analytics India, Dhruva Space.
First time a private consortium invests over ₹1,200 crore (over five years) in Indian space.
12 EO satellites with panchromatic, multispectral, hyperspectral and SAR (radar) sensors.
To be developed and operationalised by 2029 (official statement of August 12, 2026).
Aim: reduce dependence on foreign satellite data; serve climate and disaster work.
u0460.trap: 'Allied Orbits' (12-satellite EO constellation) is different from Pathfinder (Pixxel–Sarvam orbital data centre).

mcq.q: How many satellites will the Pixxel-led 'Allied Orbits' consortium launch under India's EO-PPP programme (agreement of January 2026)?
mcq.why: The consortium will launch a constellation of 12 state-of-the-art EO satellites.

u0461.gist: On December 24, 2025, ISRO's LVM3-M6 placed AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird Block-2 in low Earth orbit, LVM3's heaviest payload from Indian soil.
facts: Launched December 24, 2025 by ISRO/NSIL for AST SpaceMobile (USA).
BlueBird Block-2 weighed 6,100 kg: heaviest payload launched by LVM3 from Indian soil.
Largest commercial communications satellite in low Earth orbit (223 m2 phased array).
104th launch from Sriharikota; ninth successful LVM3 mission; third dedicated commercial mission.
Aim: direct-to-mobile connectivity from space for ordinary smartphones.
u0461.trap: Ninth successful LVM3 mission overall, but only the third dedicated commercial one.

mcq.q: The BlueBird Block-2 satellite launched by ISRO's LVM3-M6 mission in December 2025 weighed about:
mcq.why: BlueBird Block-2 was the heaviest LVM3 payload from Indian soil at 6,100 kg.

u0462.gist: PM Modi inaugurated the 10th India Mobile Congress 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi; theme 'Scale Without Boundaries'.
facts: 10th edition; held October 7 to 10, 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi; PM inaugurated it on 8 October.
Organised by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI).
Theme: 'Scale Without Boundaries'.
Four pillars: Srishti, Samvardhan, Sashakt, Suraksha.
AI for Good Build-a-thon 5.0 (October 10, 2026), theme 'Creating innovative agents in 5G'.
Build-a-thon 1st prize: Team Netaxis, RVCE Bangalore.
u0462.hook: Four pillars = four S: Srishti, Samvardhan, Sashakt, Suraksha.
u0462.trap: The event ran October 7-10, but the PM inaugurated it on 8 October.

mcq.q: What was the theme of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026?
mcq.why: IMC 2026 was held under the overarching theme 'Scale Without Boundaries'.

u0463.gist: Google DeepMind's AnthroKrishi team built ALU and AMED models that turn satellite images into farm information; they began with a focus on India.
facts: Built by Google DeepMind's AnthroKrishi team; first focused on India.
ALU = Agricultural Landscape Understanding: maps field boundaries, trees, farm wells and ponds.
AMED = Agricultural Monitoring and Event Detection: tracks crop, sowing and harvesting at field level.
Outputs are free through APIs; ALU is also a layer in Google Earth.
CarbonFarm uses the ALU API with Gemini for sustainable rice farming.
u0463.hook: ALU = the Land map (where); AMED = the Events (what and when).

mcq.q: Google DeepMind's AMED model, developed for agriculture with an initial focus on India, stands for:
mcq.why: AMED stands for Agricultural Monitoring and Event Detection.

u0464.gist: Amit Shah flagged off India's first LNG-powered train from Sabarmati, Ahmedabad on September 27, 2026, to cut diesel use.
facts: Flagged off September 27, 2026 by Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah.
Inaugural route: Sabarmati to Mahesana Junction, Gujarat.
A DEMU train with two converted Driving Power Cars, each 1,400 HP.
LNG can replace up to around 40 per cent of diesel use.
Each power car has a 2,200-litre LNG tank; over 2,000 km of field trials were done.
u0464.trap: 40% is diesel replacement, not a 40% cut in emissions. LNG train = Gujarat (Sabarmati–Mahesana); hydrogen train = Haryana (Jind–Sonipat).

mcq.q: India's first LNG-powered train, flagged off on September 27, 2026, ran its inaugural journey from Sabarmati to:
mcq.why: The inaugural journey ran from Sabarmati to Mahesana Junction in Gujarat.

u0465.gist: NIELIT launched CYBER KUSHTI 2026 on August 15, 2026, a national cybersecurity and AI hackathon that rewards human judgement, not just speed.
facts: Launched August 15, 2026 by Prof. (Dr.) M. M. Tripathi, Director General, NIELIT.
Parallel technical track of the 3rd NCCDFI 2026 (cyber security and digital forensics conference).
Partners: ISAC Foundation (National Security Database); CERT-In is Knowledge Partner.
Final round 'The Kesari': November 2026 at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi; ten finalist teams.
Winner gets the title 'Cyber Kesari 2026' and a Gada; runners-up: 'Rustam' and 'Pahalwan'.
u0465.hook: Kushti (wrestling) theme: winner = Kesari with a Gada; then Rustam and Pahalwan.

mcq.q: What title will the winning team of NIELIT's CYBER KUSHTI 2026 hackathon receive?
mcq.why: The winner gets the title 'Cyber Kesari 2026' and a Gada; runners-up get Rustam and Pahalwan.

u0466.gist: The IndiaAI Mission held the AIKosh University Engagement Programme at Chitkara University, Rajpura, on 6 August 2026 to introduce students to AIKosh.
facts: Held 6 August 2026 at Chitkara University, Rajpura, by IndiaAI Mission (MeitY).
More than 250 students took part in sessions and hands-on activities.
IndiaAI Mission was approved by the Government in March 2024.
AIKosh = India's unified AI data platform, a key pillar of IndiaAI Mission.
As on October 6, 2026: 16,000+ datasets, 350+ AI models, 200+ use cases.

mcq.q: AIKosh, India's unified data platform for AI, is a key pillar of which mission?
mcq.why: AIKosh is a key pillar of the IndiaAI Mission and India's unified data platform.

u0467.gist: PM Modi inaugurated India's first indigenous hydrogen-powered train on the Jind–Sonipat section, Haryana, on 17 July 2026.
facts: Inaugurated 17 July 2026 by PM Narendra Modi on the Jind–Sonipat section (Northern Railway), Haryana.
Two 1200 kW power cars give 2400 kW; eight trailer coaches; around 2,600 passengers.
Maximum operating speed 75 kmph; design speed 110 kmph.
Runs on a Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC); gives only water vapour and heat.
Designs by RDSO; country's largest railway hydrogen storage at Jind holds nearly 3,000 kg.
Hydrogen energy 120 MJ/Kg versus diesel 43 MJ/Kg.
u0467.hook: Hydrogen 120 vs diesel 43: nearly three times the energy per kg.
u0467.trap: Operating speed 75 kmph, design speed 110 kmph: don't swap them.

mcq.q: India's first hydrogen-powered train, inaugurated on 17 July 2026, runs on which section?
mcq.why: The train was inaugurated on the Jind–Sonipat section of Northern Railway, Haryana.

mcq.q: Which type of fuel cell is the primary energy source of India's first hydrogen-powered train (2026)?
mcq.why: The primary energy source is a Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC).

u0468.gist: The first UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance was held in Geneva on July 6–7, 2026; MoS Kirti Vardhan Singh led India's delegation.
facts: Inaugural session: Geneva, Switzerland, July 6–7, 2026.
India led by Kirti Vardhan Singh, MoS for External Affairs and Environment.
Second session to be held in New York in May 2027.
A universal, multi-stakeholder UN platform; it complements, not replaces, existing initiatives.
Concerns: deepfakes swaying elections; heavy electricity and water use by AI data centres.
u0468.trap: First session in Geneva (2026); second session in New York (2027).

mcq.q: Where was the inaugural United Nations Global Dialogue on AI Governance held in July 2026?
mcq.why: The inaugural Dialogue was held in Geneva, Switzerland, on July 6–7, 2026.

u0469.gist: China's LineShine debuted at No. 1 on the 67th TOP500 list (June 23, 2026), displacing El Capitan as the world's fastest supercomputer.
facts: 67th TOP500 list announced June 23, 2026 at ISC 2026, Hamburg, Germany.
LineShine: National Supercomputing Centre in Shenzhen, China; 2.198 Exaflop/s on HPL.
First TOP500 system above two exaflops using CPUs only; draws about 42.2 megawatts.
Five exascale systems: LineShine (China); El Capitan, Frontier, Aurora (United States); JUPITER Booster (Germany).
Top Indian systems: AIRAWAT-PSAI (rank 211), Arka (219), PARAM Rudra-104 (245), Arunika (274).
PARAM Pragya, IIT Delhi Sonipat campus: opened by PM 8 August 2026; 400 A100 GPUs, 250 AI petaflops.
u0469.trap: LineShine (China) replaced El Capitan (USA) at No. 1. India's best, AIRAWAT, is only rank 211.

mcq.q: Which supercomputer debuted at No. 1 on the 67th TOP500 list released in June 2026?
mcq.why: LineShine debuted at No. 1, displacing El Capitan.

mcq.q: PARAM Pragya, an AI-oriented supercomputing facility inaugurated by PM Modi in August 2026, is installed at:
mcq.why: The facility is installed at IIT Delhi's Sonipat campus in Haryana.

u0470.gist: The foundation stone of India's first advanced 3D chip packaging unit, by 3D Glass Solutions, was laid in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.
facts: Project: Heterogeneous Integration Packaging Solutions, promoted by 3D Glass Solutions.
Location: Bhubaneswar, Odisha; total investment ₹1,943.53 crore.
Not a chip-making fab: a greenfield advanced packaging and glass-substrate ATMP unit.
One of 12 plants approved under the scheme (others include Tata's fab and Micron's unit).
Odisha: first State with both India's first compound semiconductor fab and a 3D glass-substrate packaging unit.
u0470.trap: It is a packaging unit, not a chip fabrication plant.

mcq.q: India's first advanced 3D chip packaging unit based on glass substrates is being set up in which city?
mcq.why: The foundation stone of the unit was laid in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

u0471.gist: MeitY and Drone Federation India launched NIDAR 2.0 (2026–27) on July 13, 2026 under the SwaYaan initiative to boost student drone innovation.
facts: Launched July 13, 2026 in hybrid mode at Electronics Niketan, New Delhi.
NIDAR = National Innovation Challenge for Drone Application and Research; second edition.
Flagship of the SwaYaan initiative; called India's largest drone innovation challenge.
Focus moves to autonomous systems, indigenous avionics, navigation and core drone parts.
Also: Bharat Innovates 2026 held in Nice, 14-16 June 2026, with 120 Indian DeepTech innovators.

mcq.q: NIDAR 2.0, launched by MeitY and Drone Federation India in July 2026, is the flagship platform of which initiative?
mcq.why: NIDAR is the flagship innovation platform of the SwaYaan initiative.

u0472.gist: Pralhad Joshi launched the Green Hydrogen Certification Portal of India (GHCI) on June 17, 2026 to certify India's green hydrogen digitally.
facts: Launched June 17, 2026 by Pralhad Joshi, Minister of New and Renewable Energy.
Launched at an MNRE national workshop on strengthening the National Green Hydrogen Mission.
Developed by the National e-Governance Division (NeGD) for MNRE.
Digital backbone of the Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India.
National Green Hydrogen Mission was launched in January 2023.

mcq.q: Which body developed the Green Hydrogen Certification Portal of India (GHCI), launched in June 2026?
mcq.why: The platform was developed by the National e-Governance Division (NeGD) for MNRE.

u0473.gist: India's 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam reached first criticality on 6 April 2026, entering stage two of the nuclear programme.
facts: PFBR at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu: first criticality on 6th April 2026.
500 MWe reactor built by BHAVINI (Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Limited).
India enters the second stage of its three-stage nuclear power programme (Homi Jehangir Bhabha's vision).
India will be only the second country after Russia to run a commercial fast breeder reactor.
Also: NIELIT–Andhra Pradesh MoU (20 February 2026) for India's first Quantum-AI university campus at Amaravati.
u0473.hook: Breeder = stage 2 of 3: the breeder 'breeds' the second stage.
u0473.trap: Criticality means the chain reaction has started; full commercial operation comes later.

mcq.q: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor that attained first criticality on 6 April 2026 is located at:
mcq.why: The PFBR is at Kalpakkam in Tamil Nadu, built by BHAVINI.

mcq.q: Once the PFBR is fully operational, India will be only the second country to operate a commercial fast breeder reactor after:
mcq.why: India will become the second country in the world after Russia.

u0474.gist: At the Bharat Bodhan AI Conclave 2026 (Bharat Mandapam, February 12-13), Shri Pradhan launched the Bodhan AI Centre of Excellence and the Bharat EduAI Stack.
facts: Bharat Bodhan AI Conclave 2026: two-day event at Bharat Mandapam, February 12-13, 2026.
Shri Pradhan launched the Bodhan AI Centre of Excellence (CoE in AI for Education).
Anchor: IIT Madras; centre set up as the IIT Madras Bodhan AI Foundation.
Supported by the Ministry of Education; built as Sovereign Digital Public Infrastructure.
Bharat EduAI Stack: open-source AI infrastructure for AI tutors, teacher training, administration, policy.
u0474.trap: Bodhan AI (education, IIT Madras) is different from BODH (health AI benchmarking, IIT Kanpur).

mcq.q: Which institution is the institutional anchor of the Bodhan AI Centre of Excellence for education launched in 2026?
mcq.why: IIT Madras is the anchor; the centre is the IIT Madras Bodhan AI Foundation.

u0475.gist: India hosted the India-AI Impact Summit at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on February 16-21, 2026, the first such summit hosted by a Global South nation.
facts: Held February 16-21, 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
First time hosted by a Global South nation.
Three Sutras: People, Planet and Progress; seven Chakras (areas of cooperation).
Official logo identity: the Ashoka Chakra.
Global AI Impact Commons launched with 80+ impact stories from 30+ countries.
India AI mission GPUs: target 10000, now 38000; target of 570 Data Labs.
u0475.hook: 3 Sutras = 3 P (People, Planet, Progress); 7 Chakras turn them into action.
u0475.trap: Three Sutras vs seven Chakras: don't swap the counts.

mcq.q: Which three 'Sutras' guided the India-AI Impact Summit 2026?
mcq.why: The Summit was guided by the Sutras of People, Planet and Progress.

mcq.q: The official logo of the India-AI Impact Summit 2026 was based on which emblem?
mcq.why: The official logo's identity was the Ashoka Chakra.

u0476.gist: On October 12, 2026, J.P. Nadda laid the foundation of ICMR's first Centre for High Altitude Medicine at Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh.
facts: Foundation stone: October 12, 2026, by Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda.
ICMR's first dedicated Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research.
Location: Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti district, Himachal Pradesh.
Will study how mountain conditions and climate change affect health, especially of high-altitude and tribal people.

mcq.q: ICMR's first dedicated Centre for High Altitude Medicine and Public Health Research (foundation laid October 2026) is located at:
mcq.why: The foundation stone was laid at Keylong in Lahaul and Spiti district, Himachal Pradesh.

u0477.gist: J.P. Nadda inaugurated Aarogya Manthan 2026 on September 25, 2026, marking 8 years of AB PM-JAY and 5 years of ABDM.
facts: Inaugurated September 25, 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, by J.P. Nadda.
Organised by the National Health Authority (NHA).
Marks 8 years of AB PM-JAY and 5 years of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).
Launched: NHPR Mobile App, NHCX guide for payers, Model Digital Health Facility guidebook.
Secure Data Environment (SDE) app built by NHA with IISc Bengaluru.
u0477.trap: 8 years = PM-JAY; 5 years = ABDM. Don't swap.

mcq.q: Aarogya Manthan 2026 marked how many years of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)?
mcq.why: It marked 8 years of AB PM-JAY and 5 years of ABDM.

u0478.gist: The International Society of Blood Transfusion recognised JAMA as the 49th human blood group system (ISBT 049), announced on September 14, 2026.
facts: JAMA = 49th human blood group system, numbered ISBT 049.
Ratified at the ISBT Kuala Lumpur Congress 2026; announced September 14, 2026.
Found by UK and Israel researchers studying an Israeli woman and her brother.
Her antibody reacted with most people's red blood cells, but not with hers or her brother's.
JAMA is a separate antigen-based system, not a new type beside A, B, AB and O.
u0478.trap: JAMA is a blood group system (the 49th), not a fifth blood type next to A, B, AB and O.

mcq.q: JAMA, recognised by the International Society of Blood Transfusion in 2026, is which number human blood group system?
mcq.why: ISBT recognised JAMA as the 49th human blood group system (ISBT 049).

u0479.gist: WHO validated Bhutan's elimination of dog-transmitted human rabies on September 4, 2026, the first in the WHO South-East Asia Region.
facts: Validated by WHO on September 4, 2026.
Bhutan: first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to achieve this.
No human death from dog-mediated rabies since June 2023.
WHO lists Bhutan, Chile and Mexico as the three validated countries.
WHO criteria (2018): at least two years with no such deaths, plus capacity to stop re-emergence.
Dogs cause up to 99% of human rabies; global plan aims to end deaths by 2030.

mcq.q: In September 2026, which country became the first in the WHO South-East Asia Region to be validated for eliminating dog-transmitted human rabies?
mcq.why: WHO validated Bhutan's elimination on September 4, 2026, a first in the region.

u0480.gist: President Droupadi Murmu inaugurated 'Saushrutam 2026' at the All India Institute of Ayurveda, New Delhi, on July 15, 2026 (Sushruta Jayanti).
facts: Inaugurated July 15, 2026 (Sushruta Jayanti) at AIIA, New Delhi, by President Droupadi Murmu.
She also opened an AI-enabled 3 Tesla High-Field MRI facility at AIIA.
NCISM study on careers of women Ayurveda graduates was released.
Experts from nine countries; topics: Shalya Tantra, Kshara Sutra, Agnikarma, integrative oncology.
Acharya Sushruta: 'father of surgery in ayurveda'; author of the Sushruta Samhita.

mcq.q: 'Saushrutam 2026', inaugurated by the President on Sushruta Jayanti, was held at:
o: All India Institute of Ayurveda, New Delhi
mcq.why: The President inaugurated Saushrutam 2026 at the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi.

u0481.gist: J.P. Nadda launched Aarogya Setu 2.0 on 29 June 2026 as a Personal Health Record app under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission.
facts: Launched 29 June 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, by J.P. Nadda.
Redesigned as a Personal Health Record (PHR) app under ABDM.
The original Aarogya Setu was built during COVID-19 for contact tracing.
New features: ABHA creation, AI digitisation of lab reports, PM-JAY Wallet, empanelled hospital search.
Launched alongside: Ayushman App, NHCX, Ayushman Sarathi WhatsApp chatbot, e-Sushrut Clinic, UHI, BHTS.
u0481.trap: Old Aarogya Setu = COVID contact tracing; Aarogya Setu 2.0 = personal health record app.

mcq.q: Aarogya Setu 2.0, launched in June 2026, has been redesigned to work mainly as a:
mcq.why: It will function as a Personal Health Record (PHR) application under ABDM.

mcq.q: Which WhatsApp chatbot, launched alongside Aarogya Setu 2.0 on 29 June 2026, provides PM-JAY services?
mcq.why: The Ayushman Sarathi WhatsApp Chatbot provides PM-JAY services.

u0482.gist: The Health Ministry held the 10th National Summit on Innovation and Inclusivity in Chandigarh (30 April–1 May 2026), inaugurated by J.P. Nadda.
facts: 10th National Summit on Innovation and Inclusivity: Chandigarh, 30 April to 1 May 2026.
Organised by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; inaugurated by J.P. Nadda.
States and UTs showed health innovations and best practices.
Swasth Bharat Portal: one-stop platform putting national health programmes on one interface.
JANANI (Journey of Antenatal, Natal and Neonatal Integrated Care): ABDM-aligned RMNCH+A data platform.

mcq.q: The 10th National Summit on Innovation and Inclusivity on India's health future (2026) was held in:
mcq.why: It was organised in Chandigarh from 30 April to 1 May 2026.

u0483.gist: ICAR and ICMR jointly launched Mission SEHAT on 11 May 2026 in New Delhi to turn farm progress into better health.
facts: SEHAT = Science Excellence for Health through Agricultural Transformation.
Launched 11 May 2026 in New Delhi by J.P. Nadda and Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
Joint mission of ICAR (agriculture research) and ICMR (medical research).
Goal: 'Healthy Food, Healthy Farms and a Healthy India'.
u0483.hook: SEHAT joins Farm (ICAR) with Health (ICMR): two 'IC_R' councils.

mcq.q: Mission SEHAT, launched in May 2026 to link agriculture with health, was jointly launched by ICMR and:
mcq.why: The mission was jointly launched by ICAR and ICMR.

u0484.gist: CDSCO's expert committee recommended Takeda's TAK-003 (Qdenga) dengue vaccine for people aged 4 to 60 years in India.
facts: Subject Expert Committee (SEC) under DCGI recommended TAK-003 (Qdenga) for ages 4 to 60.
Made by Takeda Pharma, a Japanese company.
Live-attenuated (weakened virus) vaccine for dengue serotypes 1, 2, 3 and 4; DENV2 backbone.
Schedule: 2 doses, three months apart.
NCVBDC: 2,89,235 cases and 485 deaths (2023); 1,21,824 cases and 131 deaths (2025).
u0484.trap: Qdenga is the brand name; TAK-003 is the code; Takeda is Japanese.

mcq.q: Takeda's dengue vaccine TAK-003 (Qdenga), recommended by the expert committee in India, is cleared for which age group?
mcq.why: The SEC cleared it for individuals aged 4 to 60 years.

u0485.gist: On 17 February 2026, at the India AI Impact Summit, India launched SAHI and BODH to make AI in healthcare safe and ethical.
facts: Launched 17 February 2026 at the India AI Impact Summit 2026.
SAHI = Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India: national guidance framework.
BODH = Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI.
BODH built by IIT Kanpur with the National Health Authority; tests AI models without sharing data.
Atal Innovation Mission (NITI Aayog) launched the book 'AI-Preneurs of India' on 45 AI startups.
u0485.hook: SAHI = the rules (Strategy); BODH = the test (Benchmarking).
u0485.trap: BODH (health AI, IIT Kanpur) is different from Bodhan AI (education, IIT Madras).

mcq.q: BODH, the health AI benchmarking platform launched in February 2026, was developed by the National Health Authority with:
mcq.why: BODH was developed by IIT Kanpur in collaboration with the National Health Authority.

u0486.gist: Amit Shah laid the foundation of a BSL-4 Bio-Containment Facility at GBRC, Gandhinagar, on 13 January 2026: India's first state-funded BSL-4 lab.
facts: Foundation stone laid 13 January 2026 by Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
Location: Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC), Gandhinagar.
BSL-4 = highest level of biological containment, for deadly pathogens like Ebola, Nipah, Marburg.
India's only functional civilian BSL-4 lab now: National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune.
u0486.trap: Existing civilian BSL-4 lab = NIV Pune; new state-funded one = GBRC Gandhinagar.

mcq.q: India's first state-funded BSL-4 laboratory, whose foundation stone was laid in January 2026, is coming up at:
mcq.why: The BSL-4 facility is at the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre, Gandhinagar.

u0487.gist: WHO's Global TB Report 2025 (November 12, 2025) shows India carries 25% of the world's TB burden but cut incidence by 21% since 2015.
facts: Released November 12, 2025; data from 184 countries and areas.
2024: 10.7 million people got TB worldwide (131 new cases per 100,000).
India's share 25%, the highest; then Indonesia (10%) and Philippines (6.8%).
India's incidence fell 21%: 237 per lakh (2015) to 187 per lakh (2024); global fall only 12%.
India's TB mortality fell from 28 to 21 per lakh (2015 to 2024).
Treatment coverage rose from 53% (2015) to over 92% (2024); 26.18 lakh patients diagnosed in 2024.
u0487.hook: '21' twice for India: incidence fell 21%, and deaths are now 21 per lakh.
u0487.trap: 21% = India's fall in incidence; 12% = global fall. India's share of burden = 25%.

mcq.q: According to the WHO Global TB Report 2025, by how much did TB incidence in India fall between 2015 and 2024?
mcq.why: India's TB incidence fell by 21%, from 237 to 187 per lakh population.

mcq.q: As per the WHO Global TB Report 2025, India's share of the global TB burden is:
mcq.why: India (25%) tops the list, followed by Indonesia (10%).

u0488.gist: India launched a free nationwide HPV vaccination campaign for 14-year-old girls on 28 February 2026 from Ajmer, Rajasthan, to prevent cervical cancer.
facts: Launched 28 February 2026 from Ajmer, Rajasthan; covers all 36 States and UTs.
Target: girls aged 14; about 1.2 crore benefit every year (RGI 2021 estimate).
Single dose of 0.5 ml, intramuscular, in the left upper arm; free and voluntary with parental consent.
Campaign mode for three months (90 days), then on routine immunisation days.
Registration on U-WIN platform; vaccine stocks managed on the e-VIN portal.
Cervical cancer: second most common cancer among Indian women (GLOBOCAN 2022).
u0488.hook: HPV drive: age 14, one dose, 1.2 crore girls a year.
u0488.trap: U-WIN = registration and records; e-VIN = vaccine stock and logistics.

mcq.q: India's nationwide free HPV vaccination campaign (February 2026) was launched from which city?
mcq.why: The campaign was launched on 28 February 2026 from Ajmer, Rajasthan.

mcq.q: The nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched in 2026 targets girls of which age?
mcq.why: It targets 14-year-old girls across all 36 States and UTs.

u0489.gist: ICMR's Regional Medical Research Centre, Bhubaneswar, has developed AdFalciVax, a low-cost recombinant multi-stage malaria vaccine candidate stable at room temperature.
facts: Developed by the Regional Medical Research Centre (RMRC), Bhubaneswar, of ICMR.
Recombinant multi-stage vaccine candidate against Plasmodium falciparum; aims to cut infection and community transmission.
By June 17, 2026: licensed to five Indian companies; still preclinical (TRL 4), not yet approved.
Stays effective up to 12 months at normal room temperature, so no costly cold chain is needed.
Estimated cost only ₹20 per dose, versus ₹250 to ₹830 for existing vaccines.
WHO-recommended vaccines now: RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) and R21/Matrix-M; India targets zero indigenous cases by 2027, elimination by 2030.
u0489.hook: AdFalciVax: ₹20 a dose, 12 months without a fridge.
u0489.trap: AdFalciVax is only a candidate (preclinical); the vaccines already in use are RTS,S and R21.

mcq.q: AdFalciVax, a multi-stage malaria vaccine candidate, was developed by ICMR's Regional Medical Research Centre located in:
mcq.why: It was developed by the Regional Medical Research Centre (RMRC), Bhubaneswar, of ICMR.

mcq.q: What is the estimated production cost per dose of ICMR's malaria vaccine candidate AdFalciVax?
mcq.why: AdFalciVax costs about ₹20 per dose, against ₹250 to ₹830 for existing vaccines.

u0490.gist: Ahuti Mk II, an electric multirotor interceptor drone by Hyderabad's Apollyon Dynamics, recorded a test speed of 498 km/h (confirmed 29 August 2026).
facts: Built by Apollyon Dynamics, Hyderabad startup from the BITS Pilani Hyderabad Campus ecosystem.
Recorded test speed 498 km/h; confirmed 29 August 2026, entry published 1 September 2026.
Beat the previous benchmark of 325 km/h by 173 km/h.
Production interceptors target about 400 km/h operational speed.
Founders: Jayant Khatri and Sourya Choudhury; ₹2 lakh prototype grant from BITS Pilani SOLVE.
u0490.trap: 498 km/h = record by the test platform; about 400 km/h = target for production interceptors.

mcq.q: Ahuti Mk II, an Indian electric interceptor drone that set a speed record in 2026, recorded a test speed of:
mcq.why: Ahuti Mk II achieved a recorded test speed of 498 km/h.

u0491.gist: On May 13, 2026, SAMEER and ISRO's ISTRAC agreed to build deep-space X-band amplifiers using indigenous GaN chips from DRDO's GAETEC.
facts: Agreement May 13, 2026: SAMEER and ISRO's ISTRAC; GaN chips from GAETEC, DRDO.
GaN (Gallium Nitride): semiconductor for high-frequency, high-power uses.
One 3.5 × 3 mm GaN chip can deliver up to 30 watts.
DRDO's SSPL makes 4-inch Silicon Carbide (SiC) wafers and GaN HEMTs up to 150 watts.
GaN-on-SiC MMIC production at GAETEC, Hyderabad; iDEX contract with Agnit Semiconductors.
Uses: radars, electronic warfare, communications, surveillance (ISR) and unmanned systems.

mcq.q: Which DRDO laboratory has developed indigenous processes to make 4-inch Silicon Carbide (SiC) wafers for GaN technology?
mcq.why: The Solid State Physics Laboratory (SSPL) of DRDO developed these processes.

u0492.gist: INS Mangrol, the third ASW Shallow Water Craft built by Cochin Shipyard, was commissioned on 12 October 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai.
facts: Commissioned 12 October 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai; presided by Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan.
Third ASW-SWC (Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft) built by Cochin Shipyard Limited, Kochi.
Named after Mangrol town, Junagadh district, Gujarat; revives minesweeper INS Mangrol (M85), served till April 7, 2004.
Over 80% indigenous; Abhay sonar, torpedoes, Maareech torpedo decoy; waterjet propulsion.
ASW-SWC programme: 16 vessels, eight from CSL Kochi (Mahe class) and eight from GRSE Kolkata.
Mahe class commissioning: INS Mahe (24 November 2025), INS Malvan (22 July 2026), INS Mangrol.
u0492.trap: Mangrol (Gujarat town; commissioned Mumbai) vs Malvan (Maharashtra town; commissioned Karwar).

mcq.q: INS Mangrol, commissioned into the Indian Navy in October 2026, is named after a coastal town in which district?
mcq.why: Mangrol is a coastal town and fishing harbour in Junagadh district, Gujarat.

mcq.q: Which was the first ship of Cochin Shipyard's Mahe class to be commissioned (24 November 2025)?
mcq.why: Order: INS Mahe (24 November 2025), INS Malvan, then INS Mangrol.

u0493.gist: Noida-based IG Defence completed a flight trial of KAL, an indigenous long-range one-way attack drone, at Pokhran Field Firing Range, Rajasthan.
facts: Developed by IG Defence, a private firm headquartered in Noida.
Flight trial at Pokhran Field Firing Range, Rajasthan.
KAL: long-range one-way attack system for autonomous strike missions.
Declared range up to 1,000 km; endurance 7-8 hours.
Maximum take-off weight 200 kg; carries a 50 kg high-explosive warhead.
Speed: cruise 160 km/h, maximum 200 km/h; flies up to 5,000 m above sea level.
u0493.hook: KAL: made in Noida (UP), tested at Pokhran, reaches 1,000 km.

mcq.q: KAL, described as India's first indigenous long-range attack drone, was developed by IG Defence, a company headquartered in:
mcq.why: IG Defence is a private defence technology company headquartered in Noida.

mcq.q: What is the manufacturer-declared range of IG Defence's KAL long-range attack drone?
mcq.why: The declared range is up to 1,000 km, with 7-8 hours endurance.

u0494.gist: Azad Engineering, Hyderabad, delivered India's first indigenous 350 kg-thrust expendable turbojet engine, designed by DRDO's GTRE, on July 22, 2026.
facts: Designed by DRDO's Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE).
Industry partner: Azad Engineering, Hyderabad, which manufactured and assembled it.
Delivered to GTRE on July 22, 2026.
First indigenous expendable turbojet engine of the 350 kg thrust class.
Shows DRDO–private industry teamwork; may cut imports of compact propulsion systems.

mcq.q: Which company manufactured India's first indigenous 350 kg-thrust expendable turbojet engine designed by DRDO's GTRE (2026)?
mcq.why: GTRE chose Azad Engineering, Hyderabad, which delivered the engine on July 22, 2026.

u0495.gist: India Optel Limited launched indigenous 'GARUD' high-resolution binoculars for civilians on August 13, 2026 at DPSU Bhawan, New Delhi.
facts: Launched August 13, 2026 at DPSU Bhawan, New Delhi, with Dr Garima Bhagat present.
IOL: Mini Ratna Category-I Defence PSU under the Department of Defence Production.
Made by Ordnance Factory, Dehradun, a unit of IOL.
Features: 8x magnification, 7.6-degree field of view, ±5 diopter, about 610 grams.

mcq.q: The 'GARUD' high-resolution binoculars launched for the civilian market in August 2026 were developed by which unit?
mcq.why: GARUD was developed and made by Ordnance Factory, Dehradun, a unit of India Optel Limited.

u0496.gist: Bengaluru's Astrobase Space Technologies unveiled EVEREST on August 7, 2026, described as India's first privately built Full-Flow Staged Combustion rocket engine.
facts: Unveiled August 7, 2026 by Astrobase Space Technologies, Bengaluru.
FFSC = Full-Flow Staged Combustion: fuel and oxidiser go through separate pre-burners.
India's first LOX-methane high-thrust engine; fourth commercial FFSC globally (after SpaceX, Stoke Space, LandSpace).
Could support reusable launches of up to 30 tonnes to low Earth orbit.
As of August 22, 2026, full hot-fire testing was pending; figures are design targets.
u0496.trap: Performance figures are company design targets; the engine was not yet fully hot-fire tested.

mcq.q: EVEREST, unveiled in August 2026 as India's first privately developed FFSC rocket engine, was built by:
mcq.why: Bengaluru-based Astrobase Space Technologies unveiled EVEREST on August 7, 2026.

u0497.gist: Cochin Shipyard launched Machilipatnam (BY 529), seventh vessel of its eight-ship Mahe-class ASW Shallow Water Craft series, at Kochi on July 29, 2026.
facts: Launched July 29, 2026 at Kochi by Mrs Goolrukh Anand; Vice Admiral Atul Anand present.
Yard number BY 529; seventh in CSL's eight-ship Mahe-class series.
Named after Machilipatnam, port city and HQ of Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh.
Roles: coastal anti-submarine warfare, underwater surveillance, mine-laying; over 80% indigenous.
Contract for eight vessels signed April 30, 2019; whole programme: 16 ASW SWCs (CSL Mahe + GRSE Arnala).
u0497.trap: 'Seventh' is its building order, not the seventh commissioned. Launched is not the same as commissioned.

mcq.q: Machilipatnam (BY 529), launched by Cochin Shipyard in July 2026, is named after a port city in which state?
mcq.why: Machilipatnam is the historic port city and headquarters of Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh.

u0498.gist: INS Malvan, the second Mahe-class ASW Shallow Water Craft built by Cochin Shipyard, was commissioned at Karwar on July 22, 2026.
facts: Commissioned July 22, 2026 at Karwar.
Second of eight ASW-SWCs built by CSL, Kochi; sixth of 16 ASW-SWCs commissioned.
Named after Malvan, a coastal town in Maharashtra linked to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
Crest: 'Bagh Nakha' (Tiger's Claw); motto: 'Silent Claws'.
Over 80 percent indigenous content.
u0498.hook: Malvan → Shivaji → Bagh Nakha (tiger's claw) → motto 'Silent Claws'.
u0498.trap: Second of CSL's eight, but sixth of all 16 ASW-SWCs to be commissioned.

mcq.q: What is the motto of INS Malvan, commissioned into the Indian Navy in July 2026?
mcq.why: The ship's motto is 'Silent Claws'; its crest carries the Bagh Nakha.

u0499.gist: Pune's Nibe Limited demonstrated Garudastra, a 120 mm vehicle-mounted long-range mortar, to the Indian Army at Infantry School, Mhow, on June 17, 2026.
facts: Demonstrated June 17, 2026 at the Infantry School, Mhow, to the Indian Army.
Maker: Nibe Limited, Pune, with a foreign original equipment manufacturer (OEM).
A 120 mm mortar mounted on a mobile vehicle.
Shown on a No Cost–No Commitment (NC-NC) basis.
Offers fast mobility, high firepower, quick deployment and withdrawal.

mcq.q: Garudastra, demonstrated to the Indian Army at Mhow in June 2026, is a vehicle-mounted mortar of which calibre?
mcq.why: Garudastra is a 120 mm mortar mounted on a mobile vehicle platform.

u0500.gist: The Coast Guard (Bharatiya Tatrakshak) commissioned ICGS Akshay, a new-generation Fast Patrol Vessel built by Goa Shipyard Limited, on June 27, 2026.
facts: Commissioned June 27, 2026 at Goa Shipyard Limited, Goa.
Type: new-generation Fast Patrol Vessel (FPV).
'Akshay' means Indestructible.
Roles: law enforcement, coastal security, search and rescue, marine environment protection.
Designed and built by Goa Shipyard Limited: Aatmanirbhar Bharat.
u0500.trap: Akshay = 'Indestructible' (June 2026); Achal = 'firm' (May 2026). Both are Goa Shipyard patrol vessels.

mcq.q: What does the name of ICGS Akshay, the Fast Patrol Vessel commissioned in June 2026, mean?
mcq.why: Akshay means 'Indestructible'.

u0501.gist: Microsoft, Singtel, Tata Communications and Lightstorm will build I-2SEA, a submarine cable linking India, Malaysia and Singapore; contracts signed July 2, 2026.
facts: Consortium: Microsoft, Singtel, Tata Communications and Lightstorm.
Lightstorm announced construction contracts on July 2, 2026.
Links India's east coast to Singapore and Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur).
Two landings in India: Machilipatnam (shortest access to Hyderabad) and South Chennai.
About 3,600 km long from Singapore to Machilipatnam.
NEC Corporation is system supplier; ASEAN Cableship is marine installation partner.

mcq.q: The I-2SEA submarine cable (contracts signed in July 2026) will land at which Indian town to give the shortest subsea access to Hyderabad?
mcq.why: The landing at Machilipatnam will provide the shortest subsea access to Hyderabad.
